questions.prompt: Your DSL users complain that a missing semicolon produces `Syntax error near EOF` 200 lines later. What architectural fix solves this?

options.text: Synchronization-point error recovery in the parser plus tracking exact token spans on every AST/error

questions.prompt: When designing a **domain-specific type system** (e.g., physical units `meters` vs `seconds`), what is the biggest win?

options.text: Invalid domain combinations (adding meters to seconds) fail at compile time instead of causing silent runtime disasters

questions.prompt: Match each compiler architecture decision to its engineering trade-off.

rows.label: Building an External DSL with custom parser
Building an Internal DSL in host language
Targeting LLVM IR vs. custom x86 emitter

columns.label: Full control over syntax and error messages, higher tooling cost (LSP, formatter)
Instant reuse of host IDE/debugger/package manager, constrained by host syntax
World-class optimizations and multi-arch targets, heavier build dependency and compile time

questions.prompt: Why is **LSP (Language Server Protocol)** support often decisive for external DSL adoption?

options.text: Developers expect autocomplete, go-to-definition, and inline diagnostics in their editor from day one

questions.prompt: Which principles keep a **compiler codebase** maintainable as the language grows? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Separating passes cleanly (lex -> parse -> resolve -> typecheck -> lower -> codegen)
Desugaring complex surface forms early into a small, well-typed core IR
Maintaining comprehensive golden tests and fuzzers for every pass
Mutating global parser state from codegen

questions.prompt: What is **multi-level IR** (like MLIR)?

options.text: Allowing progressive lowering through domain-specific dialects (e.g., tensor -> affine loops -> LLVM) instead of dropping straight to low-level IR

questions.prompt: Why do **GPU DSLs** (like Triton) operate on **tiles/blocks** rather than individual scalar threads?

options.text: Block-level abstractions let the compiler coalesce global memory loads, manage shared SRAM, and schedule tensor cores automatically

questions.prompt: In **LLVM IR** / SSA optimization, why can **aliasing** (two pointers possibly referring to the same memory) block optimization?

options.text: If `*p` and `*q` might alias, the optimizer cannot safely reorder loads/stores or cache values in registers
Pointers cannot be stored in RAM

questions.prompt: What is **escape analysis** in a managed-runtime compiler?

options.text: Determining if a newly allocated object never outlives its creating function/thread so it can be stack-allocated or scalar-replaced

questions.prompt: Which trade-offs matter when choosing **AOT compilation** vs. **JIT compilation**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: JIT can specialize hot code using runtime profile feedback (devirtualization, branch frequencies)
JIT adds warmup latency and runtime memory for the compiler itself
AOT programs cannot run on Linux
AOT gives instant startup and predictable memory with zero runtime compiler overhead

questions.prompt: Why should **sandboxed DSLs** (e.g., user-submitted filter expressions or rule engines) avoid `eval()` in a general host language?

options.text: Unrestricted `eval()` allows arbitrary code execution, infinite loops, and filesystem/network access

questions.prompt: What is **fuel / step-budget metering** in an embedded rule-engine VM?

options.text: Decrementing a counter per instruction/loop so untrusted user scripts terminate cleanly if they exceed their budget

questions.prompt: Match each solver/constraint DSL problem to the right tool.

rows.label: Combinatorial graph/scheduling with rules and defaults
Integer/linear scheduling across multiple backend solvers
Bayesian posterior inference over continuous parameters

questions.prompt: In **OCaml**, why is using a **visitor or catamorphism** / **recursive AST pass** with immutable nodes safer than mutating ASTs in place?

options.text: Immutable AST passes never corrupt shared subtrees or leave half-transformed state if an error occurs

code.source:
let rec map_expr f = function
  | Add (a, b) -> f (Add (map_expr f a, map_expr f b))
  | e -> f e

questions.prompt: What is **Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO)**?

options.text: Feeding real-workload execution profiles back into the compiler so it optimizes hot paths, inlining, and branch layout

questions.prompt: Which checks prevent **soundness bugs** in a compiler's optimizer? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Formalizing or property-testing algebraic rewrite rules
Disabling all assertions in debug builds
Writing an IR verifier/type-checker that runs after *every* optimization pass
Differential testing `-O0` (unoptimized) vs `-O2` (optimized) outputs on generated programs

questions.prompt: Why do **hardware description languages (Verilog)** require **testbenches and cycle-accurate simulation** before FPGA synthesis?

options.text: Synthesis/place-and-route takes minutes to hours, and hardware bugs after tape-out are vastly harder to inspect than software bugs

questions.prompt: What is **decompilation / round-trip pretty-printing** useful for when testing a parser?

options.text: Parsing `src -> AST -> pretty_print -> AST2` and verifying structural equivalence catches missing precedence or parentheses bugs

questions.prompt: In **language versioning**, what is an **edition** mechanism (like Rust editions)?

options.text: Allowing opt-in surface syntax changes per crate/module while all editions compile to the same IR and interoperate seamlessly

questions.prompt: What is **monomorphization** (used in Rust/C++/Julia) vs. **type erasure / boxing** (used in Java/OCaml)?

options.text: Monomorphization generates specialized machine code per concrete type (zero runtime overhead, larger code); erasure shares one compiled body

questions.prompt: Which factors determine whether to **compile a DSL** vs. **interpret it**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Whether the language name starts with a vowel
How often each script runs (one-off config vs. hot inner loop)
Whether target environments allow JIT/native code generation (e.g., restricted mobile/sandboxed hosts)

questions.prompt: What is **incremental / query-based compilation** (e.g., Salsa / Rustc)?

options.text: Recompiling everything from scratch on every keystroke
Memoizing fine-grained compiler queries by input dependencies so editing one function only recomputes affected checks

code.source: type query_key = Parse of file_id | TypeCheck of def_id

questions.prompt: In **OCaml**, why do compiler writers often separate **Untyped AST** from **Typed AST (TAST)**?

options.text: Subsequent lowering passes can assume every expression carries a verified type without re-checking or handling unresolved names

code.source: type typed_expr = { node: expr_kind; ty: typ; span: loc }

questions.prompt: What is **inlining**'s classic trade-off?

options.text: Eliminating call overhead and enabling cross-function optimization, at the risk of code bloat and instruction-cache misses if overused

questions.prompt: Match each DSL domain to the primary hazard it must prevent.

columns.label: Unbounded joins/regexes causing DoS or injection
Non-deterministic evaluation causing spurious production diffs
Unintended inferred latches or clock-domain crossing metastability

questions.prompt: Why should **configuration DSLs** usually avoid full Turing completeness?

options.text: Turing completeness is slower to parse
Non-Turing-complete config languages guarantee termination, stay statically analyzable, and resist hidden side effects

questions.prompt: What is **link-time optimization (LTO)**?

options.text: Deferring whole-program IR optimization and cross-module inlining until all object files are linked together

questions.prompt: In **Datalog**, what is **semi-naive evaluation**?

options.text: Evaluating recursive rules using only newly derived delta facts from the previous iteration instead of re-scanning all facts

questions.prompt: What is **algebraic effect / capability** tracking in modern language design?

options.text: Tracking I/O, state, or exception effects in function types so pure code and effectful boundaries stay explicit

questions.prompt: Which practices make **DSL error messages** genuinely helpful to domain experts? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Showing the exact source line with an underline caret pointing at the offending span
Explaining the violation in domain terms rather than internal parser state names
Suggesting a likely fix ('did you mean ...?') when a symbol is close
Printing only `Error 42` with no line number

questions.prompt: Why do **scientific DSLs** (Julia, Stan, R) invest heavily in **interoperability with C/Fortran**?

options.text: Decades of battle-tested BLAS/LAPACK numerical kernels already exist in C/Fortran

questions.prompt: What is **tree-shaking / dead-code elimination** in bundle-oriented DSLs?

options.text: Pruning unreferenced definitions from the final output based on a static reachability graph

questions.prompt: In **LLVM**, what is **scalar replacement of aggregates (SROA)**?

options.text: Breaking non-escaping structs/aggregates into individual scalar SSA registers so memory loads/stores disappear

questions.prompt: In OCaml, what does this **tail-recursive** evaluator pattern avoid?

options.text: Stack overflow on deeply nested sequential statements

code.source:
let rec run env = function
  | [] -> env
  | s :: rest -> run (step env s) rest

questions.prompt: What is **fuzzing with grammar-aware generators** (e.g., Csmith / grammar mutators)?

options.text: Generating syntactically and semantically valid random programs to stress-test middle-end optimizers and codegen

questions.prompt: Why is **determinism** (identical inputs -> identical outputs, no random hash-map iteration order in codegen) critical in compilers?

options.text: Non-deterministic symbol/output order breaks build caching, reproducible builds, and debugging

questions.prompt: Which signs indicate a **DSL has outgrown its original design** and needs refactoring? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Ad-hoc special cases piling up in the parser and type checker
Performance cliffs because the IR lowered too early
Clean, composable small core with good test coverage
Users resorting to fragile string-templating hacks to work around missing abstraction

questions.prompt: What is **partial evaluation / staging**?

options.text: Specializing a general interpreter with respect to a known static program/input at compile time to remove interpretation overhead
Running half of a test suite

questions.prompt: Why should **runtime errors** in a DSL (division by zero, out-of-bounds) still carry source-location metadata or stack traces?

options.text: Users need to know which line of *their* DSL script failed, not just an internal VM instruction offset

questions.prompt: What is **bootstrap** in compiler engineering?

options.text: Writing a language's compiler in the language itself and compiling it with an earlier version

questions.prompt: When designing **standard library / built-ins** for a DSL, why keep the core small and composable?

options.text: Small orthogonal primitives compose cleanly and keep the spec, tests, and optimizer tractable

questions.prompt: What is the hallmark of **great language & DSL engineering**?

options.text: Clear domain fit, unambiguous grammar, sound semantics, helpful diagnostics, clean IR lowering, and thorough differential/fuzz testing
Inventing new syntax for every problem regardless of cost
